Borrowed from German Polymer, from Ancient Greek πολύς (polús, “many”) + μέρος (méros, “part”). Compare Russian полиме́р (polimér), Belarusian паліме́р (palimjér).

Borrowed from German Präparat, from Latin praeparātiō.

parole.significato: press (the print-based media (both the people and the newspapers))
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Presse, from French presse. Compare Russian пре́сса (préssa), Belarusian прэ́са (présa).

parole.significato: food, foodstuffs, food supplies, provisions, victuals (edible stores for future use)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Proviant. Compare Russian провиа́нт (proviánt), Belarusian правія́нт (pravijánt).
Borrowed from German produktiv via Russian продукти́вный (produktívnyj) or Polish produktywny.

Borrowed from German Pudel.

parole.significato: punch (a hot alcoholic beverage made from wine, rum, fruit juice, sugar or honey, and hot water and spices)

parole.significato: pyrotechnics (the art and technology of fireworks and related military applications)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from German Pyrotechnik, ultimately from Ancient Greek πῦρ (pûr) and τέχνη (tékhnē). Compare Russian пироте́хника (pirotéxnika), Belarusian піратэ́хніка (piratéxnika), Polish pirotechnika.

parole.significato: Reich, a German empire; specifically the Third Reich (Nazi Germany)

parole.significato: resident (a diplomatic representative who resides in a foreign country, usually of inferior rank to an ambassador)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Resident, from French résident.

parole.significato: flight (a specific journey made by an aircraft)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Reise.

parole.significato: Reich, a German empire; specifically the Third Reich (Nazi Germany)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Reich (“empire, realm”).

parole.significato: Reichstag (the lower chamber of the federal parliament of Germany until 1945)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Reichstag.

parole.significato: formulation, formula (of a medicine, food product, etc.)

parole.significato: scepticism, scepsis (UK), skepticism, skepsis (US) (a studied attitude of questioning and doubt)

parole.significato: chisel (tool consisting of a slim oblong block of metal)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Stemmeisen.

parole.significato: statics (the branch of mechanics concerned with forces in static equilibrium)

parole.significato: syringe (a medical instrument for injecting or drawing off liquid)

parole.significato: state (a political division, e.g. a US state)

Probably borrowed from German Illustrator, from Latin illūstrātor. Compare Russian иллюстра́тор (illjustrátor), Belarusian ілюстра́тар (iljustrátar).

parole.significato: implant (anything surgically implanted in the body, such as a tissue graft or prosthesis)
parole.testo: Probably from German Implantat, ultimately from Latin implantātus. Compare Russian импланта́т (implantát).
Borrowed from German Impuls, from Latin impulsus. Compare Russian и́мпульс (ímpulʹs).
Probably borrowed from German Immunität, ultimately from Latin immūnitās. Compare Russian иммуните́т (immunitét), Belarusian імунітэ́т (imunitét), Polish immunitet.
Borrowed from German Invalide or French invalide, from Latin invalidus.
Borrowed from German Ingenieur, from French ingénieur, from Latin ingenium. Compare Russian инжене́р (inženér), Belarusian інжыне́р (inžynjér), Polish inżynier.

parole.significato: private business deal, especially a speculative one; gesheft
